rule.borderline_note: The hardest calls are umbrella against component and national scheme against a state's listing of it. Both are decided the same way every time and the reasoning is on each row, so a reader can flip one and rerun.
rule.scope_note: Soundness is about identity only. Nothing here reads or weighs an audit finding: the question asked of every pair is whether the report is ABOUT this scheme, never what it concluded.
rule.sound: the registry entry names the programme the report audited, and the entry's jurisdiction is one the report covers. A union audit of a national scheme may match a state's listing of that same national scheme, because the register deliberately under-merges and one scheme can hold several rows.
rule.wrong: anything else: the entry is a budget head, a body, a ministry or an accounting line rather than a scheme; the entry is a component, a sibling, a successor or an award attached to the audited scheme rather than the scheme itself; the entry is a different state's scheme that happens to share a generic name; or the join is matcher noise with no relation between the two names.

what: Hand labels for every join between a CAG audit subject and a registry entry. Ground truth for parse/cag_join.py. This is a census and not a sample: all 398 joins the matcher produces are labelled, so precision is a count. Audit and correct these; the rule is only as good as they are.
